dominant_emotion: defeated resignation shading into shame — 'it's impossible, the market left me behind' — the quiet grief of watching ownership (and the stability/dignity/future it stands for) close in your own city while peers build equity
core_wound: permanent exclusion / being locked out for good — 'I'll be a renter forever, priced out of belonging and a future in the place I already live.' Abandonment + loss: the American-dream door closing in your face.
pain_to_promise_gap: 'I'll never be able to afford a home in the SFV' → 'you can realistically own here in months, not years — with a fraction of the cash you think you need — once someone shows you which doors are actually open to you.'

market_beliefs.external_problem: Homes cost too much ($1M+), interest rates are too high (6.51%), and I don't earn enough — so it's just not possible for me right now.
market_beliefs.internal_problem_UMP: You've been sold the 20%-down myth (~$200k+) and told you need 'perfect' conditions. The real problem isn't the price — it's that nobody has shown you which of the stacked assistance programs you personally qualify for, so you self-disqualify before you ever apply.
market_beliefs.external_solution: Save for years to hit 20% down, wait for prices to 'crash,' or give up and keep renting indefinitely.
market_beliefs.internal_solution_UMS: The SFV has 5+ stackable down-payment + closing-cost assistance programs (CalHFA, LAHD LIPA up to $161k, LACDA HOP80/HOP120, Greenline up to $35k) layered on top of 3.5%-down FHA — a guided, income-matched path that gets you in the door with a small fraction of the cash, not a 7-figure savings account.

mechanism_rationale: Evocative + constraint-baked: a 'side door' you can actually walk through (vs the locked 20%-down front door), and 'stacked' encodes the real mechanism (layering multiple assistance programs). Passes the portability test — it's specific to the SFV-assistance reality, not droppable into another market.
identity_ceiling: Renters who believe ownership is years away or permanently out of reach — pitch to 'own within months with the cash you have now,' NOT 'build a real-estate empire.' Meet the identity at 'I could actually be a homeowner,' which is already a stretch for this market.
top_voc_soundbites: The market is just too expensive, it's impossible.
I can't afford the monthly payments with these interest rates.
There's nothing good available in my price range/desired area.
I'm competing against all-cash buyers and investors.
The process is too complicated and overwhelming.
I went through a first time homebuyers program and they offered me down payment assistance and they didn't give me all the money they said.
I don't want to buy a 'fixer-upper' and incur more costs.

grounded_facts.dpa_programs: CalHFA; LAHD LIPA up to $161,000; LACDA HOP80/HOP120; Greenline up to $35,000
grounded_facts.entry_neighborhoods: Reseda, Van Nuys, Chatsworth, Granada Hills, Northridge

ejection_triggers_do_not_say: Do NOT promise 'free house' / 'no money down ever' (DPA has income caps + some have shared-appreciation clauses — overpromising trips the BS detector and echoes the 'they didn't give me all the money' burn).
Do NOT shame them for renting or 'not trying hard enough.'
Do NOT say 'just buy a fixer-upper' (explicit stated aversion).
